subject: Edge handoff -> asymmetric NAT translations causing session failures
messages:
From: Jim Walters <jim.w@edgegrid.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, partners@cloudswitch.io
Cc: ops@edgegrid.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent session failures after on-prem handoff (logs attached)

Hi Rohan,

We started seeing intermittent TCP session failures for traffic from our internal clients to services hosted in Redwood Private on Friday evening. Symptoms: client logs show TCP FIN/RST with no application-layer error, while the server side logs show connections from a different source port/IP than the client.

Attached: flowlogs-edgegrid-20260830.log — shows multiple short-lived sessions where the source IP/port changes mid-session.

We run a pair of customer-edge devices doing SNAT for outbound traffic; traffic then hits Redwood front-door (private front proxy) which also performs a source rewrite for policy reasons. On a sample trace the return path appears to flow back to a different egress IP, causing sessions to break.

Can you confirm whether there was any configuration change on the Redwood perimeter that could cause an extra SNAT or asymmetric routing? This is impacting a handful of customers (we'll share prefixes). We're available to provide tcpdumps, traceroutes, and times.

--
Jim Walters
EdgeGrid Network Ops

messages_3:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent session failures after on-prem handoff (logs attached)

Quick triage notes from the perimeter perspective (preliminary):

1) Look for asymmetric routing: if the return path hits a different NAT device we can lose conntrack state. Request customer's traceroute from affected clients to service and traceroute from service to client.

2) Common on-prem misconfig: two-stage SNAT (customer edge SNAT -> Redwood perimeter SNAT) where ephemeral ports are not preserved or translation overlaps. This appears consistent with the logs Jim shared.

3) MTU / fragmentation: If DF is set and packets are getting fragmented or blackholed, that can cause incomplete TCP handshakes and retries. Check for ICMP fragmentation-needed messages. Suggest setting MTU clamp to 1420 on the customer edge while we diagnose.

Commands to gather:
- sudo tcpdump -nne 'host <client-ip> and host <server-ip>' -w /tmp/eg-affected.pcap
- sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
- sudo cat /proc/net/ip_conntrack | grep <client-ip>

Temporary mitigations:
- Reserve a dedicated SNAT range at the customer edge and add an allow/passthrough rule on our perimeter for that range (avoid rewriting).
- If sticky SNAT is supported, configure session pinning for the affected prefix.

I attached a quick topology diff (topology-diff-edgegrid.png) showing where double translation could occur.

-Laura
Network Engineering
messages_4:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, ops@edgegrid.com, partners@cloudswitch.io
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent session failures after on-prem handoff (logs attached)

I pulled the pcap Jim provided (trace-20260830.pcap) and ran a quick analysis. Findings:

- The three sample flows show client -> customer-edge (SNAT to 203.0.113.45), then flow hits Redwood front-door which rewrites source to 10.244.1.21 (internal rewrite for policy). The return flow sometimes returns to 203.0.113.46 (a different egress IP) which means the second SNAT on the return doesn't match conntrack.

- We also see occasional PMTU Path MTU Discovery failures: a handful of SYN packets have DF set and ICMP frag-needed replies are being dropped somewhere on the return path. That can exacerbate connection instability.

Immediate recommended fix (short-term):
1) EdgeGrid: allocate a /29 SNAT range and announce it from your edge; ensure customer-edge preserves source port mapping.
2) Redwood: add a perimeter passthrough rule for that /29 (no SNAT) and carve it into a canary route table so only affected prefix uses it. This prevents the second source rewrite.
3) Both: temporarily clamp MTU to 1420 on customer-edge to eliminate fragmentation as a variable while we test.

Longer term: evaluate implementing sticky SNAT on Redwood perimeter for sessions associated with Private deployments and add route pinning to keep return path consistent.

I can prepare the perimeter ACLs and a rollout playbook; will need a 30-minute maintenance window to apply the canary and verify. Attaching the annotated pcap snippet for your team.

-Marissa
Private Deployments

- Root cause (probable): asymmetric routing combined with two-stage SNAT causing conntrack mismatch; MTU/fragmentation is a contributing factor in some flows.
- Short-term plan: EdgeGrid to allocate a dedicated SNAT /29 and enable MTU clamp to 1420. Redwood will add a canary passthrough for that /29 (no SNAT) and apply only to the affected tenancy.
- Rollout: we propose a 30-minute maintenance window tomorrow 2026-08-31 09:30-10:00 PDT to apply the canary rule and monitor. If you confirm the /29 and provide the traceroute outputs, our ops team will stage the ACL and a rollback plan.

If you want immediate assistance, we can open a live bridge during the window. Jonas will be on-call for the actual perimeter change and Marissa will validate captures post-change.

Thanks — please confirm the /29 and the preferred window.
